summary: The article, dated September 15, 2023, examines how small businesses struggle to build an online presence and digital marketing strategy as the field evolved from 1990s websites and email to SEO, social media, content marketing, data-driven ads and CRM. It draws on local owners and experts who describe the complexity, constant content demands and cost of skills and tools. It concludes that digital marketing is now a necessity, and that small businesses' adaptability will shape the market's future.
one_line: Small business owners and experts describe the challenges and necessity of building an online presence and digital marketing strategy in 2023.
key_facts: Digital marketing began for small businesses in the late 1990s and early 2000s during the dot-com boom, when websites served as online brochures and email marketing emerged.
Jessica Malloy owns 'Bloom Haven,' a boutique floral shop opened in July 2024, and says digital marketing is now about mastering SEO, decoding analytics and building a digital personality.
SEO specialist Mark Fulbright says keeping up with algorithm changes is a full-time job and that local SEO can mean the difference between being found by your community or being invisible.
In a survey conducted on October 1, 2023, 75% of small business owners felt overwhelmed by the demands of social media management.
Elise Hawthorne, owner of the pet grooming service 'Proper Paws,' finds juggling Instagram stories, Facebook posts and TikTok daunting as a solo entrepreneur.
Digital strategist Darren Lee says consistently providing valuable content builds trust and establishes authority in the market.
Advertising has shifted from print and broadcast to Facebook Ads, Google AdWords and influencer partnerships, and data analytics now allows precise targeting and retargeting.
On November 3, 2023, a workshop for local businesses covered advertising changes, where Alexei Petrov argued even small businesses must use data analytics to get measurable results.
Samantha Hui, owner of the artisan coffee shop 'Gusto' that opened in June 2024, says translating personal touch into the digital world has been her biggest learning curve.
CRM software lets small businesses nurture leads and build loyalty through personalized interactions at scale, but integrating it takes time and effort.
Enrolment in local workshops, online courses and community college digital marketing classes has risen, according to Thomas Keller, a marketing professor at the Regional Community College.
The article names budget constraints, shifting consumer behaviors and rapid technological change as key difficulties, and calls a robust online presence a necessity rather than a luxury.
